claims.text: A uniform nanometer-scale distribution of SRO precipitates in an insulating or semiconducting crystalline matrix will significantly reduce lattice thermal conductivity.
The proposed matrix conducts heat predominantly through lattice vibrations and has minimal free-electron heat conduction.
The as-prepared matrix contains little to no nanometer-scale SRO precipitates.
Tailored thermal treatments or composition tuning can introduce a controlled, uniform distribution of nanometer-scale SRO precipitates.
Phonon conduction dominates under the proposed room-temperature to moderately elevated-temperature conditions.
Nanoscale SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces the phonon mean free path.
Enhanced phonon scattering caused by SRO precipitates reduces phonon lifetime or scattering time.
A reduced phonon lifetime lowers lattice thermal conductivity.
Using an insulating or semiconducting matrix minimizes electronic contributions and isolates the lattice thermal-conductivity response.
The precipitate-containing material will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than the same matrix without engineered SRO precipitates.
The thermal-conductivity reduction is expected to be significant.
The baseline material without a uniform SRO-precipitate distribution has less phonon scattering.
The proposed causal interpretation requires grain-boundary and non-SRO defect scattering to remain constant between samples.
The magnitude of the conductivity change may depend on precipitate size, spacing, and interface quality.
TEM or HAADF-STEM can characterize or confirm nanoscale precipitates and their distribution.
Annealing above the precipitate dissolution temperature can produce a control with minimized or dissolved SRO precipitates.
Statistically indistinguishable conductivity, or higher conductivity in the precipitate-containing sample, would falsify the stated directional hypothesis.
